# Margin

**An AI coding agent that knows what a fix will cost before it starts, controls its spend while it works, and only bills when the repository's own tests prove the fix.**

Margin takes a GitHub issue, quotes a price band from what similar jobs cost before, fixes the issue under a hard spending cap, and judges
the result with the project's test suite. A fix counts only if the failing tests now pass and nothing that passed before has broken. The
customer pays the quoted price for a verified fix and nothing otherwise, so every run ends with a receipt that shows the quote, the real
cost and the margin.

Built during neatHack 2026 (10 and 11 October) with [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com), [Entire](https://entire.io),
[cfo.ai](https://cfo.ai) and [TypeSafe](https://typesafe.ai).

---

## The problem

AI agents can fix real bugs, but nobody can price that work:

- **Cost is unpredictable.** The same agent spent $0.06 on one issue and $0.30 on another in our benchmark, and a failed attempt still
  costs money.
- **Failure is expensive and quiet.** A naive agent fixed 8 of 12 real issues; the 4 it failed still cost $0.77, and two of those ended
  with a test that had passed before now failing.
- **Agents waste money after the work is done.** Verified runs kept going after their tests passed: 18% of their spend came after the fix
  had already verified.
- **There is no proof of value.** An agent's "I fixed it" is not evidence, so outcome-based pricing (pay per fix) is too risky to offer.

## What Margin does

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Screen** | An intake gate (TypeSafe's Jev) checks the issue before any money is spent: is it a real, fixable defect, or text trying to instruct the agent? |
| **Quote** | A cost band and a price, learned from past jobs with similar features (issue size, code-graph reach, repository size, test time). |
| **Govern** | A spending cap from the quote, a governor that reacts at 60% and 85% of it, and a coach model that steps in when the agent is stuck. |
| **Verify** | The repository's tests decide. Test files and test infrastructure are restored before judging, a probe makes sure pytest is the real one, and a test that passed before and now fails, is skipped or goes missing counts against the fix. |
| **Prove** | A receipt and a ledger row for every run: quote, price, actual cost, verdict, revenue and margin, with a trace of every turn in neatlogs. |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    I[GitHub issue] --> G{Intake gate}
    G -- declined --> X[Nothing spent]
    G -- accepted --> Q[Quote: cost band and price]
    Q --> R[Agent run under a spend cap]
    R -- stuck --> C[Coach note]
    C --> R
    R --> V{Repository tests}
    V -- verified --> B[Bill the quoted price]
    V -- not verified --> N[Bill nothing]
    B --> L[(Receipt and ledger)]
    N --> L
```

## Results

Five versions of the agent ("arms") were run on the same **12 evaluation issues** from 8 open-source Python libraries (cachetools, toolz,
more-itertools, sqlparse, tomlkit, tabulate, marshmallow and mistune), one run each, with the same worker model (`claude-haiku` through the
event's proxy). Four more issues were used only to calibrate. Every number below is regenerated from the stored ledger by `make verify`.

| Arm | What it adds | Fixed | Cost per verified fix | Gross margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | naive agent: whole files as context, flat price | 8 of 12 | $0.261 | 13% |
| B | code-graph context (entire-graph) and test feedback | 11 of 12 | $0.109 | 64% |
| C | B plus the quote and the spend governor | 9 of 12 | $0.129 | 63% |
| D | C plus a coach when stuck, stop when verified, a `run_python` tool, lessons from past jobs | **11 of 12** | **$0.107** | **70%** |
| E | D plus TypeSafe's Jev deciding when to coach, which lessons to use, and which issues to accept | **11 of 12** | **$0.108** | **69%** |

Full tables, per task: [`docs/results.md`](docs/results.md). Every claim with its evidence: [`EVIDENCE.md`](EVIDENCE.md).

## Impact

Measured on this benchmark (12 tasks, one run each, so read the differences as indicative):

- **59% cheaper per verified fix** than the naive agent ($0.261 to $0.107), with three more issues fixed (8 to 11 of 12) and gross margin
  from 13% to 70%.
- **91% fewer tokens in the first model call** on the same issue: 33,582 for the naive agent against 2,916 with code-graph context.
- **Spend after the fix had verified fell from 18% to 5%**, because the run now stops once the tests prove the fix.
- **Bad jobs are stopped before they cost anything.** On held-out items the intake gate accepted 12 of 12 genuine issues and declined 6 of
  6 issues with a planted instruction to the agent and 4 of 4 vague ones, for about $0.00005 per issue.
- **Cheap judgment, used where it matters.** Letting Jev decide when to coach cut coaching spend by about 30%, and all of Jev's judging
  for 12 jobs cost under one cent.
- **Quotes you can price on.** In a leave-one-out check the actual cost fell inside the quoted band for 14 of 16 tasks.
- **Failures recover.** An injected flaky test, a test timeout, an API overload and a `kill -9` mid-run each ended in a verified fix, and the
  killed run resumed from its checkpoint with its spend counted once ([`docs/evidence/failure-recovery.md`](docs/evidence/failure-recovery.md)).

What did **not** work is reported too: the quote and governor alone (arm C) did not beat plain graph context, and Jev (arm E) made the agent
cheaper to supervise but did not raise the fix rate ([`docs/notes/`](docs/notes/)).

## Use cases

Margin fits any agent work that a machine can check, because that is what makes "pay only if verified" possible.

- **Outcome-priced coding services.** An agency or bot quotes each issue, caps its spend, and bills only when CI passes.
- **Maintenance at scale.** Dependency upgrades, security patches, flaky tests, lint and type debt: thousands of small, verifiable jobs where
  the margin on each one decides whether the service is profitable.
- **Cost control for a company's agent fleet.** Budgets per team, a receipt per job, stuck-run detection, and chargeback from real costs.
- **Bounties.** Set a bounty from the quote band and pay out on verification.
- **Beyond code.** Data fixes checked by validation rules, SQL fixes checked against expected results, configuration changes checked by
  policy, documentation fixes checked by link checkers.

The business plan built in cfo.ai from these measured costs is in [`docs/business/`](docs/business/).

## How it is built

| Tool | What it does in Margin |
|---|---|
| [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com) | A trace of every run: each turn, model call, tool call, governor decision and recovery, tagged by arm, task and version. |
| [Entire](https://entire.io) | entire-graph is the agent's code search and impact analysis; Entire checkpoints record the build sessions ([public checkpoint](https://entire.io/gh/JemIIahh/margin/commit/5ad9776bfaa59fb58de2c6bb05778623b56fd78d)); Entire Brain holds durable facts about the project. |
| [cfo.ai](https://cfo.ai) | The business plan: pricing, costs, revenue and runway from the measured unit economics. |
| [TypeSafe](https://typesafe.ai) | Jev answers typed yes/no questions with calibrated probabilities: the intake gate, the progress judge and the lesson picker. |
| Models | The worker is `claude-haiku` and the coach `claude-sonnet-4.6`, through the event's LiteLLM proxy; the Anthropic API is also supported. |

Every arm's thresholds were set on the four calibration tasks only and frozen before the evaluation runs
([`docs/notes/tuning.md`](docs/notes/tuning.md), [`docs/notes/judge-calibration.md`](docs/notes/judge-calibration.md),
[`docs/notes/intake-calibration.md`](docs/notes/intake-calibration.md)).

## Try it without any keys (about 5 minutes)

Checked on a fresh clone with no `.env`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/JemIIahh/margin.git && cd margin
uv sync
make verify                                 # 374 tests, offline; regenerates docs/results.md from the stored ledger and checks it
uv run margin quote --task tabulate-241     # free, no model call: the price band, learned from the published ledger
open docs/receipts.html                     # one card per recorded run, verified and not verified
```

`margin quote` prints `cost band $0.0668 - $0.4451 (p50 $0.1724) from 15 past runs; price $0.6677` for that task. It needs `git`, `uv`,
network access (it clones the open-source project) and the [Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.io) for the graph step; without Entire, the tests
that need it are skipped rather than failed.

## Setup and run

```bash
uv sync                                  # Python 3.12 is pinned
cp .env.example .env                     # then fill in the keys; never commit .env
```

`.env` needs one model provider: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (the default), or `MARGIN_PROVIDER=litellm` with `LITELLM_API_KEY` and
`LITELLM_BASE_URL` for an OpenAI-compatible proxy, with `MARGIN_MAINbench:

Cair 💧

The payout route a chatbot can't get wrong.

An agent that plans how a prize or client payment reaches your bank account: it refuses routes that can't deliver, fills W-8BEN line 10 only when a treaty article really applies, computes the most that can land, and shows the source of every figure. Every plan is a neatlogs trace.


[![Live App](https://img.shields.io/badge/🚀_Live-App-06b6d4?style=for-the-badge)](https://app.cair.edycu.dev) [![Demo Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/▶_Demo-Video_2:57-FF0000?style=for-the-badge)](https://youtu.be/UC7pSo3hUlk) [![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/🌐_Site-cair.edycu.dev-1C4C9C?style=for-the-badge)](https://cair.edycu.dev) [![Pitch Deck](https://img.shields.io/badge/📊_Pitch-Deck-f59e0b?style=for-the-badge)](https://cair.edycu.dev/pitch/) [![Read the Traces](https://img.shields.io/badge/🔍_Verify-Traces-f59e0b?style=for-the-badge)](https://app.cair.edycu.dev/verify) [![For Judges](https://img.shields.io/badge/📌_Judge-Page-0f766e?style=for-the-badge)](https://app.cair.edycu.dev/judge) [![Rules Sheet](https://img.shields.io/badge/📋_Rules-Sheet-ef4444?style=for-the-badge)](https://app.cair.edycu.dev/rules) [![Built for neatHack](https://img.shields.io/badge/neatHack-Oct_10--12_2026-8b5cf6?style=for-the-badge)](https://luma.com/s5blr882)
![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python_3.12-3776AB?style=flat&logo=python&logoColor=white) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-009688?style=flat&logo=fastapi&logoColor=white) ![neatlogs](https://img.shields.io/badge/neatlogs-traces-black?style=flat) ![Entire](https://img.shields.io/badge/Entire-code_graph-black?style=flat) ![Qwen Cloud](https://img.shields.io/badge/Qwen_Cloud-615CED?style=flat) ![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-758_passing-brightgreen?style=flat) [![CI](https://github.com/edycutjong/cair/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/edycutjong/cair/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/edycutjong/cair?sort=semver)](https://github.com/edycutjong/cair/releases/latest) [![CodeQL](https://github.com/edycutjong/cair/actions/workflows/codeql.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/edycutjong/cair/actions/workflows/codeql.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

For judges · Demo & reproduce · Architecture · Metrics · Business plan

--- ## 💡 The Problem & Solution ### The Problem Prize winners and freelancers outside the US fill in a payout form once or twice a year, and the form is where the money is lost: - **An option that can't deliver.** Devpost's prize-claim help lists Wise as a payout method (the options a winner sees vary by country). Wise's own help page: *"personal Wise account holders with an address in Indonesia can no longer hold money or currencies in their account."* - **A tax line that invites a false statement.** A chatbot will happily tell you to put "Article 21" on W-8BEN line 10. The US–Indonesia treaty has 31 articles and none of them is "Other Income". - **Fees nobody quoted.** Payoneer publishes its platform receiving fee as *"Varies by marketplace"*. ### The Solution One task, end to end: *get this payout to my account intact*. In Cair the route, line 10 and every amount are decided by code from sourced rows; the model only words the card, and a provenance guardrail checks that wording. Where no primary source exists the answer is UNCLEAR, never a guess. ## 🏗️ Architecture & Tech Stack 1. **Plan** — a fixed evidence plan: what the payer offers and whether a W-8BEN applies → can each offered option receive in your country → the US-treaty position and nearest treaty articles → the ECB reference rate (USD payers) or the exchange's accepted networks (USDC payers) → Decimal arithmetic. 2. **Tools** — six tools, each a neatlogs TOOL or RETRIEVER span, reading `data/rules_sheet.csv` (every fact cell with a stated value has a primary source and a read date, [`data/sources.md`](data/sources.md); the 3 PayPal cells with no source say UNCLEAR), the treaty texts and the ECB rate. 3. **Decide** — code picks the route (never a REFUSED or UNCLEAR one) and line 10 (an article only if a sourced one covers the income). 4. **Verify** — a provenance GUARDRAIL checks the model's explanation: no figure, rate or article that isn't in a tool output, no endorsing a refused route, no article on line 10. Blocked → one retry with the findings → a template built from the tool outputs. 5. **Recover** — every tool is retried once, then a documented fallback: the last ECB rate fetched (stamped stale) or UNCLEAR. Never a model-written number. 6. **State** — the plan is stored; the user confirms each line before copying it (a confirm span in the same neatlogs session); later, the user reports what landed. 7. **Check the result** — the receipt reconciler reads Cair's own quote back from the neatlogs trace over MCP and writes an EVALUATOR span comparing it with what arrived. | Layer | Choice | |---|---| | Language / server | Python 3.12 · FastAPI · uvicorn · Jinja2, state in SQLite | | LLM | Qwen Cloud (`qwen3.8-max`, temperature 0) through the OpenAI-compatible client | | Facts | `data/rules_sheet.csv` + treaty texts (BM25 retrieval) + ECB reference rates (Frankfurter) | | Tracing | neatlogs SDK (every LLM call wrapped), HTTP `/v1/trace` write-back, MCP read-back | | Code graph | Entire `graph` (local, no egress) | | Host | EC2 behind Caddy at [app.cair.edycu.dev](https://app.cair.edycu.dev) | Full detail: [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md). ## 🏆 neatlogs, Entire & cfo.ai Integration ### neatlogs — how it was used to build and improve Cair - **Every plan is one trace**: WORKFLOW → AGENT → 6+ TOOL/RETRIEVER spans → LLM → GUARDRAIL, with session and hashed end-user bound per request. Eval runs are tagged `eval` / `v1` / `v2` / `ablation`. - **Finding failures**: `search_traces "provenance_guardrail BLOCKED"` over the MCP server returned the v2 plans whose explanation had been blocked (`evidence/traces/search-guardrail-blocked.json`, re-run later, so it also lists later blocks); `get_trace_context` showed the LLM text next to the guardrail verdict. Two real bugs came out of it (an amount in the 2000s parsed as a year; refusals that repeated the user's "0%"), both fixed and re-run. → [`evidence/rca-01.md`](evidence/rca-01.md) - **Reading results back in the product**: the receipt reconciler and the public [`/verify`](https://app.cair.edycu.dev/verify) page read traces back over MCP. First receipt: the builder's own $7,000 Devpost prize that landed (builder-reported) as $4,897 in Payoneer. Cair's quote was "at most $4,900 before the receiving fee (UNCLEAR)"; the reconciler read that bound back from the trace and recorded *within sourced bound, $3.00 not explained by the sourced rules* — a **replay of a known outcome**, not a prediction (EVALUATOR trace [`f5a47b9c…`](https://app.neatlogs.com/traces?orgId=ae155adf-dd4b-456e-a79a-b3e3324e7b81&projectId=a91f004f-568a-47ba-8990-5f10fb956af2&q=f5a47b9cba7cf056a800e136616e0013), neatlogs dashboard). - **HTTP write-back**: confirm and EVALUATOR spans are posted server-side to `/v1/trace`; the write key never reaches the browser. - The neatlogs dashboard links in this repository open the builder's project and need a neatlogs login on that organisation; the same step trees are saved as screenshots in [`docs/assets/neatlogs/`](docs/assets/neatlogs) and the trace exports read back over MCP are in [`evidence/traces/`](evidence/traces). What was hard or undocumented: [`docs/DX-REPORT.md`](docs/DX-REPORT.md). ### Entire — how it was used Entire's code graph (`entire graph`, local and no-egress) was run on this repository while building: after the year-parsing fix, `search` with a plain-language description of the bug returned the corrected rule at rank 1 and its covering test at rank 2; `impact` was run on `rail_eligibility` before the unlisted-country fix and reports 0 callers, probably because the planner passes the tools as function values (`att.call("fx_quote", tools.fx_quote, …)`), which the graph does not follow; the `fee_calc` and `figures.extract` queries returned only symbol-disambiguation lists. `diff` summarises every entity changed since the frozen set was tagged. Outputs, with the commands: [`evidence/entire/`](evidence/entire). Entire checkpoints were deliberately not enabled: `entire enable` installs coding-agent hooks and settings into the repository and checkpoints keep the agent conversation, and this repository is public. ### cfo.ai — business plan The model is entered in cfo.ai and shared publicly: **[cfo.ai/s/PQ2HUGmiJl3P0RQB](https://cfo.ai/s/PQ2HUGmiJl3P0RQB)** (5 pages: Runway, Pricing, Unit economics, Monthly costs, Revenue scenarios); the spreadsheet export is [`docs/cfo/Runway.xlsx`](docs/cfo/Runway.xlsx). Every plan is a neatlogs trace.** *The payout route a chatbot can't get wrong.* ## The 30-second path No account, no key, no clone. 1. Open the [live app](https://app.cair.edycu.dev). tool (Agent Orchestrator, Entire, neatlogs, cfo.ai, GitHub). |
| `agent/` | The CFO agent: sizing, routing, ceilings, escalation. |
| `cli/` | The `tally` command. |
| `dashboard/` | Static page that reads the ledger and run state. |
| `demo/` | Sample backlog and scripted outcomes for `tally demo`. |

## Configuration

With neatlogs on, Tally drains the completed Codex worker's hook spool from
its own process, outside the worker sandbox. It uses the official package's
spool API (there is no flush CLI), matching native session IDs or the worktree
path. Only successfully delivered batches are acknowledged; failed,
unrelated and malformed batches remain queued. A locked or incomplete drain
is reported as missing worker trace delivery. Dry runs do not drain workers.

With `integrations.entire: true`, enable Entire in the target repository and
trust its Codex hooks through `/hooks` before starting workers. Tally records
the task commit's `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer and its native `entireSessionId`
separately from the AO `sessionId`. Logs-only checkpoints retain conversation
context; escalation defaults to a metadata-only handoff containing the
checkpoint/session IDs, branch, recorded and changed files, attempt verdict,
and task text. It does not generate a summary or export a transcript.
`entire.generatedSummaries: true` explicitly opts into Entire's summary
provider (`checkpoint explain --generate`), which may export session content;
this setting is off by default and requires the user's approval.
When Tally publishes a verified branch, it also pushes the checkpoint refs
named by its new commits to `origin` and to an `entire` remote when configured.
Checkpoint upload failures are reported as publishing failures. Dry runs do
not publish branches or checkpoints.

Entire documents commit links as
`https://entire.io/gh/<org>/<repo>/commit/<commit-sha>`. Tally keeps
`checkpointUrl` null unless the CLI returns a URL; a local checkpoint does not
by itself establish that a hosted link works.

Tally assumes nothing about the repository it works on. The repository, test
command, model tiers, list prices, ceilings and budget all come from
`tally.yaml` (a tier is a name, harness, model id, provider, list price and ceiling share); see `schema/fixtures/finished-run/tally.yaml` for a complete
example and `schema/tally-config.schema.json` for the rules.

Money in the ledger and run state is stored as integer nanos of USD
(1 USD = 1,000,000,000). List-price estimates multiply aggregate tokens by the
configured rates in `tally.yaml`; they are normalized estimates, not invoices.
New ledger rows snapshot those rates in `price` and record their source and
verification status in `priceNote`. Unknown models/providers or rates that
disagree with the verified snapshot are labelled unverified. Operator-supplied
`tiers[].priceNote` is retained as a config note, not independently verified.

### Codex Tier Prices

Official base text rates checked 2026-10-11, USD per million tokens:

| Model | Input | Cached Input | Output | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| gpt-5.6-luna | 0.20 | 0.02 | 1.20 | [OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-luna) |
| gpt-5.6-terra | 2.00 | 0.20 | 12.00 | [OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-terra) |
| gpt-5.6-sol | 4.00 | 0.40 | 20.00 | [OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol) |

```yaml
tiers:
  - { name: cheap, harness: codex, sessionMode: tui, provider: openai, model: gpt-5.6-luna, price: { inputUsdPerMTok: 0.2, cachedInputUsdPerMTok: 0.02, outputUsdPerMTok: 1.2 }, ceilingFraction: 0.2 }
  - { name: middle, harness: codex, sessionMode: tui, provider: openai, model: gpt-5.6-terra, price: { inputUsdPerMTok: 2, cachedInputUsdPerMTok: 0.2, outputUsdPerMTok: 12 }, ceilingFraction: 0.5 }
  - { name: top, harness: codex, sessionMode: tui, provider: openai, model: gpt-5.6-sol, price: { inputUsdPerMTok: 4, cachedInputUsdPerMTok: 0.4, outputUsdPerMTok: 20 }, ceilingFraction: 1 }
```

Per-request prompts above 272K input tokens have input/output uplifts;
cache writes also have an uplift. AO's aggregate token buckets cannot resolve
these adjustments. Sol's published promotional rates last at least through
2026-11-21; recheck before subsequent runs. Historical costs are not repriced.

For dry runs, set `backlog.source: file` and point `backlog.file` at YAML like:

```yaml
tasks:
  - id: T1
    title: Add validation for empty player name
    size: small
    outcomes: [passed]
  - id: T2
    title: Persist settings after restart
    size: medium
    outcomes: [stopped, passed]
```

`outcomes` is optional and defaults to one passed simulated attempt.

The latest run is also mirrored to `.tally/runs/latest/run.json` and
`.tally/runs/latest/ledger.json` so the dashboard has one stable path to poll.

## Secrets

Keys live in `~/.tally/.env`, outside every repository, and are loaded from
there. Never put them in this repo; `.env` files are git-ignored.

=== hacker-git-code_underwrite- commits: first: last: authors: files: 0 toplevel: .entire/.claude/.cursor: code loc: test files: 0 X/twitter links: video links: cfo links: entire links: neatlogs links: live links: # Underwrite **A team of AI agents that does venture due diligence while you sleep, and checks its own work.** Give it a list of startups. An **analyst agent** decides what to look up, reads sources and records every fact with the exact sentence it came from; facts that don't match their source are bounced back to it on the spot. A **skeptic agent** attacks the result and sends the analyst back until the evidence holds up. A **watcher** re-checks every company each night and re-investigates only what changed. A **coach agent** reads all of this from [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com) traces, rewrites the agents' prompts, and keeps a change only if the eval score goes up. **Live site (memo gallery + scoreboard):** https://hacker-git-code.github.io/underwrite-/  ·  Built for **#neatHack** (Oct 10–12, 2026), theme: *"Build agents you'd trust to run without you watching."*

Each memo is a three-page dossier modelled on Sequoia's famous 1977 evaluation form for Apple: **page 1** an evaluation form (typed labels, hand-written answers, red circled source numbers, a VERIFIED stamp, conflicts noted in the margin), **page 2** a typed memorandum with the full analysis, **page 3** an appendix with every source, the claims it supports, the claims that were rejected, and the agent's run log. Download as PDF, or page 1 as PNG. --- ## Contents - [What it does](#what-it-does) - [Why you can trust it unattended](#why-you-can-trust-it-unattended) - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Self-improvement: the Coach and neatlogs](#self-improvement-the-coach-and-neatlogs) - [Results](#results) - [Sponsor tools and how each is used](#sponsor-tools-and-how-each-is-used) - [Quickstart](#quickstart) - [Commands](#commands) - [Configuration](#configuration) - [Running it unattended on AWS](#running-it-unattended-on-aws) - [Project layout](#project-layout) - [Evidence checklist for judges](#evidence-checklist-for-judges) - [Security and privacy](#security-and-privacy) - [Limitations and roadmap](#limitations-and-roadmap) ## What it does A real run (Ramp, agent mode), shortened: ``` $ underwrite run "Ramp" --domain ramp.com [recover ] gemini-3.8-flash failed (daily quota exhausted); falling back to gemini-3.5-flash [recover ] gemini-3.5-flash failed (daily quota exhausted); falling back to groq:openai/gpt-oss-120b [plan ] 10 questions, 20 queries for Ramp [agent ] step 1 -> company_profile() [agent ] step 2 -> record_claim(field='founded_year', value='2019', evidence_id='E1') → ACCEPTED C1 [agent ] step 4 -> web_search('Ramp founders CEO Eric Glyman Karim Atiyeh') [agent ] step 5 -> record_claim(field='ceo', 'Eric Glyman and Karim Atiyeh serve as Co-CEOs', evidence_id='E7') ... [agent ] round 1 ended on budget after 24 steps [verify ] judge: 11 supported, 0 partial, 0 rejected of 11 [skeptic ] objection: key traction numbers rely on a single low-authority source [skeptic ] objection: no evidence on risks or controversies - a priority-1 question [skeptic ] sending the analyst back for round 2 [agent ] step 25 -> web_search('Ramp customer count revenue 70,000 Bloomberg TechCrunch') [agent ] step 27 -> web_search('Ramp lawsuits controversy security incident regulatory issues') [extract ] C13 In May 2025, a Congressman investigated Ramp over its attempt to win a $25 million federal contract [verify ] claim rejected in-loop: quote not in E20 (match 53%) — agent must fix it [verify ] self-corrected: C14 accepted after the agent fixed a rejected claim [agent ] step 40 -> finish(...) [memo ] done in 212s · 15 claims · 93% supported · 11 Crustdata credits · 2 recoveries ``` Nobody told it to look for a congressional investigation: the skeptic objected that risks were unexamined, and the analyst went and found one. It also found that Ramp's CEO had just made his co-founder co-CEO, with the source linked. A first-pass diligence memo takes an analyst hours. Underwrite produces one in 3–5 minutes for about 11–19 Crustdata credits, and the LLM side runs on free tiers. ### Three agents, one loop | Agent | Decides | Guardrails around it | |---|---|---| | **Analyst** (tool-calling loop) | which tool to call next: `company_profile`, `web_search`, `read_page`, `record_claim`, `update_question`, `add_question`, `finish` | every claim is grounded against its cited source **the moment it is recorded** and bounced back if the quote isn't there; budgets shown after every action; `finish` refused while priority-1 questions are open; old page text compacted out of context; conversation checkpointed every step | | **Skeptic** | whether the evidence is good enough, or which 1–4 objections must be fixed first | sees only what an investment committee would see; can send the analyst back while rounds and budget remain | | **Watcher** (nightly) | whether a company changed since its memo (fresh Crustdata record diff + news since the memo) | re-investigation is scoped to one new priority-1 question, seeded with the previous verified claims | | **Coach** (offline) | how to rewrite the agents' prompts, based on neatlogs traces, detections and eval failures | a change is kept only if the eval improves on the train split at sane cost; test split held out | The original fixed pipeline (plan → search → extract → verify → write) is kept as `--mode pipeline`, as the baseline the agents are measured against. ## Why you can trust it unattended | Risk when nobody is watching | What Underwrite does | |---|---| | The model invents a fact | Every claim must carry a quote from one evidence block. Code checks that the quote is really in that source (fuzzy match ≥ 90%); claims that fail are rejected **without** asking a model. | | The quote exists but doesn't prove the claim | A separate judge prompt sees only the claim, the quote, and the source text around it, and rules supported / partial / unsupported. Only supported and partial claims reach the memo. | | Sources disagree | Verified values are clustered per fact (founding year, headcount, funding, HQ, CEO); more than one cluster is a **conflict**, written in red in the memo's margin (e.g. *"Crustdata says 18 employees, the website says 50"*). | | The memo cites something unverified | Citations to claims that didn't pass verification are stripped before rendering, and counted. | | An API fails (429, 5xx, timeout, empty page) | Exponential backoff with jitter, honouring `Retry-After`; Crustdata search → DuckDuckGo fallback; Crustdata fetch → direct fetch fallback. | | A model is down, overloaded, or out of quota | Each role has a chain of models across providers (Gemini → Gemini → Groq → Cerebras → Claude on Bedrock). ## Self-improvement: the Coach and neatlogs ```mermaid flowchart LR E1[Eval v1
12 companies, ground truth] --> F[Failures
train split only] N[(neatlogs)] -->|MCP: search_traces,
get_trace_context,
list_detections, triage_list| CO[Coach] F --> CO CO -->|rewrites prompt files| P2[prompts/v2] P2 --> E2[Eval v2] E2 -->|better on train, cost OK?| DEC{keep?} DEC -->|yes| ACC[accepted] DEC -->|no| REJ[rejected] ``` 1. **Measure.** `underwrite eval` runs a prompt version over 12 companies with hand-checked facts (founding year, HQ, founders, CEO) in `evals/dataset.json`, split 8 train / 4 test. It scores the memo's fact sheet against ground truth and records the agent's own trust metrics (grounding, support, coverage, conflicts, cost). 2. **Diagnose.** `underwrite coach` collects the train-split failures (wrong facts, rejected claims, unanswered questions, recovery events) and connects to the **neatlogs MCP server** to read what neatlogs saw: the span tree of the worst traces (`get_trace_context`), keyword/semantic trace search (`search_traces`), detections (`list_detections`) and suggested fixes (`triage_list`, `triage_get`). 3. **Change.** The smart model, at high reasoning effort, proposes targeted edits to the prompt files, each tied to the evidence behind it. Edits that drop a `{{placeholder}}` or the system/user separator are rejected automatically. It is told never to add company-specific facts, which would overfit the eval. 4. **Verify.** The new version is evaluated on the same companies (tool results are cached, so both versions see the same evidence), and it is **kept only if quality on the train split improves without cost rising more than 50%**. The test split is reported as the honest, held-out number. Every decision is written to `prompts/vN/COACH_NOTES.md`. ## Results The live numbers are on the [scoreboard](https://hacker-git-code.github.io/underwrite-/#scoreboard) and in `runs/eval-*/eval.json`. The v1 → v2 comparison from the Coach is in `prompts/v2/COACH_NOTES.md`. _Evaluation in progress: this table is filled in from `runs/eval-*/eval.json` once the v1 baseline and the Coach's v2 have both been scored._ ## Sponsor tools and how each is used | Tool | Used for | Where | |---|---|---| | **neatlogs** | Tracing every run (spans, prompt templates + versions, token cost, recovery log spans, sessions per batch); the **Coach reads traces, detections and triage fixes over the neatlogs MCP server** to decide how to improve the agent. | `underwrite/obs.py`, `underwrite/llm.py`, `underwrite/coach.py` | | **Entire** | Every coding-agent session that built this repo is checkpointed and linked to its commit (`Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers, refs under `refs/entire/checkpoints/`), with secrets redacted. Claude on Amazon Bedrock is supported as a provider too. | `underwrite/llm.py` | ## Quickstart Requirements: Python 3.10–3.13 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). ```bash git clone https://github.com/hacker-git-code/underwrite-.git underwrite && cd underwrite uv sync cp .env.example .env # then paste your keys (see below) uv run underwrite doctor # checks every key, model and the neatlogs MCP connection uv run underwrite run "Linear" --domain linear.app --open ``` Keys (all have free tiers): | Variable | Where to get it | |---|---| | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | https://aistudio.google.com/apikey | | `GROQ_API_KEY` | https://console.groq.com/keys | | `CRUSTDATA_API_KEY` | Crustdata dashboard | | `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` | https://app.neatlogs.com → project → API key | | `CEREBRAS_API_KEY`, `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` | optional extra fallbacks | ## Commands | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `underwrite run "Company" --domain x.com [--mode agent\|pipeline] [--open] [--chaos 0.3]` | Research one company and write its dossier | | `underwrite batch watchlist.txt [--new-only] [--limit N]` | Research a list unattended (`Company, domain` per line) | | `underwrite resume ` | Continue an interrupted run from each company's last saved phase / agent step | | `underwrite watch [--limit N]` | Re-check researched companies; re-investigate only what changed | | `underwrite eval --prompts v1 [--split train\|test\|all]` | Score a prompt version against ground truth | | `underwrite coach --base v1` | Improve the prompts from neatlogs traces + eval failures, evaluate, keep or reject | | `underwrite compare pipeline:v1 agent:v1 [--split test]` | Before/after table between two evals (`[mode:]version`) | | `underwrite rescore ` | Re-grade a finished eval after a ground-truth fix, using the memos it already wrote | | `underwrite render [--open]` | Re-draw dossiers (HTML + PDF) without re-running the agent | | `underwrite site [--open]` | Build the website in `docs/` (merges with what's already published) | | `underwrite doctor` | Check keys, models, Crustdata balance and the neatlogs MCP connection | ## Configuration All optional, set in `.env`: | Variable | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `UW_MODELS_SMART` | `gemini:gemini-3.8-flash,gemini:gemini-3.5-flash,groq:openai/gpt-oss-120b,…` | Planner/writer/coach model chain | | `UW_MODELS_FAST` | `gemini:gemini-3.5-flash-lite,gemini:gemini-3.1-flash-lite,groq:openai/gpt-oss-20b,…` | Extractor/judge model chain | | `UW_PROMPTS` | `v1` | Prompt version to run | | `UW_MAX_SEARCHES` / `UW_RESERVE_SEARCHES` | `10` / `2` | Web searches per company, and how many are held for the gap round | | `UW_MAX_FETCHES` / `UW_PAGE_CHARS` | `8` / `4000` | Pages fetched per company, characters kept per page | | `UW_MAX_ROUNDS` | `2` | Research rounds per company | | `UW_MAX_CREDITS_PER_RUN` | `400` | Stop a batch after this many Crustdata ## Evidence checklist for judges - [ ] **Before/after with numbers**: [Results](#results), `prompts/v2/COACH_NOTES.md`, `underwrite compare v1 v2` - [x] **neatlogs traces**: every run is a trace in the project; ids are printed by each run and in each dossier's appendix - [x] **Entire checkpoints**: `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers on commits; `entire checkpoint list` in a clone - [ ] **cfo.ai business plan**: `business/PLAN.md` + cfo.ai model - [x] **A failure the agent recovered from**: see the `[recover]` lines in any run's `events.jsonl`, and the chaos run - [ ] **Public posts tagged #neatHack**: linked from `hackathon.md` - [x] **Public repo with commits dated during the hackathon**: this repository ## Security and privacy - API keys live only in `.env` (git-ignored). The repo history, every tracked file and every Entire checkpoint were scanned for the real key values: none present. Entire also redacts secrets from checkpoint transcripts. - Web content is untrusted: prompts tell the models to ignore instructions found in evidence; the dossier escapes all model and web text and renders only `http(s)` links (tested). - The direct page fetcher refuses any URL (including after redirects) that resolves to a non-public address, so it can't be pointed at the cloud metadata service (tested). - Raw page text (`state.json`) and PDFs stay out of git; # neatHack 2026 — Underwrite

## Project

**Underwrite** — an autonomous due-diligence agent you can leave running overnight.
Give it a list of startups; it plans the research, pulls company data from Crustdata,
searches and reads the web, extracts every factual claim with a source, has an
independent verifier check each claim against the source text, flags contradictions
(e.g. "website says 50 people, Crustdata says 18"), and writes a cited investment memo
as a three-page paper dossier (HTML, PDF, PNG).

A **Coach** loop reads the agent's own neatlogs traces, detections and triage fixes
over the neatlogs MCP server, rewrites the agent's prompts, re-runs the eval set,
and only keeps a change if the numbers improve.

- Challenge: "Build agents you'd trust to run without you watching." (single track)
- Required tools: neatlogs (tracing + Coach loop), Entire (checkpointed build sessions), cfo.ai (business plan)
- Repo: https://github.com/hacker-git-code/underwrite-
- Live site: https://hacker-git-code.github.io/underwrite-/ (after GitHub Pages is enabled)

## Team

- Rehan Momin (solo)

## Stack

- Python 3.12, uv
- LLMs (free tiers): Gemini 3.8 Flash / 3.5 Flash / 3.5 Flash-Lite / 3.1 Flash-Lite, Groq gpt-oss-120b / 20b;
  Claude on Bedrock supported but not used (the AWS allowance covers EC2/Lambda only)
- Data: Crustdata (company enrich, web search, web fetch, credit balance)
- Observability: neatlogs Python SDK + neatlogs MCP (Coach)
- Build provenance: Entire CLI (checkpoints on every commit, secrets redacted)
- Hosting: GitHub Pages (site) + AWS EC2 t3.small (nightly runner)

## Build log

### 2026-10-10

- Read hackathon page, neatlogs SDK/MCP docs, Entire CLI README, Crustdata API docs.
- Chose idea: due-diligence agent + self-improving Coach loop.
- Installed Entire CLI 0.11.4, `git init`, `entire enable --agent claude-code`.
- Built v0 (commit `5b0a6b0`): planner → researcher → extractor → verifier → replanner → writer; checkpointed
  state machine with `resume`; chaos mode; eval harness (12 companies, train/test split); Coach over neatlogs MCP.
- Found the AWS check-in page only approves EC2/Lambda/IAM/LB, not Bedrock → switched LLMs to free Gemini + Groq
  behind a provider fallback chain (commit `56d3dc2`). Gemini 2.5 models are closed to new keys → Gemini 3.x defaults.
- First real run (Razorpay): accurate but thin; found the search budget was spent on 4 of 8 questions. Fixed with
  breadth-first queries + 2 searches reserved f

# Niyam

**When the law changes, the code changes with it.**

Niyam (Hindi and Marathi for "rule") is an AI agent that reads new government orders and keeps welfare eligibility rules, written as code, in sync with the law. Every rule links to the clause it came from, every change is tested and independently verified, and the agent's full reasoning is saved with the change.

Built during [neatHack 2026](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon) by team USV.

| | |
|---|---|
| Website | **[usv240.github.io/niyam](https://usv240.github.io/niyam/)** (GitHub Pages) and **[34-227-135-194.sslip.io](https://34-227-135-194.sslip.io/)** (AWS) |
| Live API and watcher | AWS EC2 t3.small in Hackathon_VPC, us-east-1: `https://34-227-135-194.sslip.io/api/v1/health` |
| Demo video | *added on submission day* |
| Rulebook maintained by the agent | [usv240/niyam-rulebook](https://github.com/usv240/niyam-rulebook) |
| Showcase pull request opened by the agent | [usv240/niyam-rulebook#2](https://github.com/usv240/niyam-rulebook/pull/2) |
| Entire checkpoint on that change | `01M4JDH944E4HPRCA4WKDJTFN7` (commit `2d67c14`) |
| Build log | [hackathon.md](hackathon.md) |

## The problem, in one paragraph

In India, eligibility for welfare is decided by software: portals, field-worker apps, helplines, chatbots. The law behind it is published as PDF Government Resolutions (GRs), mostly in Marathi in Maharashtra, and it changes often. Nobody keeps the code in sync. When code drifts from the law, people are wrongly excluded or wrongly paid: in Telangana an eligibility algorithm cancelled more than 1.8 million food cards ([Al Jazeera and Pulitzer Center, 2024](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2024/1/24/how-an-algorithm-denied-food-to-thousands-of-poor-in-indias-telangana)), and nobody affected could see why.

## What Niyam does

```
Watch -> Triage -> Extract -> Encode -> Verify -> Resolve -> Publish
```

1. **Watch** the public list of new Maharashtra GRs every 15 minutes (never the CAPTCHA-protected search, never bypassing anything).
2. **Triage** with a fast model: does this order change a covered scheme?
3. **Extract** every eligibility change with the exact Marathi quote, page and clause. Each quote is checked against the PDF; invented quotes and wrong numbers are rejected.
4. **Encode**: Claude Code edits the rulebook in its own git worktree, adds dated values (history is never overwritten), and writes test citizens at every limit. It never sees the raw PDF, only the checked change list.
5. **Verify**: a separate agent on a different model, blind to the code change, writes its own test citizens from the law. They are run against the new rules.
6. **Resolve**: a coordinator settles disagreements, sends precise fixes, or asks a human a plain-English question.
7. **Publish**: a pull request with quotes, verification, confidence and reasons. Entire links the coding agent's session to the commit as a checkpoint. It merges on its own only when the [trust policy](web/app/trust/page.tsx) allows: numbers or dates only, every check agrees, confidence at least 0.90, and nobody loses eligibility.

## Results (measured, small sample)

Six evaluation cases: the real 3 July 2024 Ladki Bahin amendment, the same order as a scan with no text layer, two real unrelated GRs, and two synthetic robustness tests labelled as synthetic inside the PDF (a pure benefit increase, and a hidden prompt injection).

| Metric | v1 | v2 | v3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Changes found, values, boundaries | 100% | 100% | 100% |
| Test citizens get the right answer | 97.6% | 100% | **100%** |
| Correct choice to act alone or ask a human | 67% | 100% | **100%** |
| Independent verifier agrees | 95.7% | 100% | **100%** |
| Cost per document | $0.88 | $0.29 | **$0.13** |
| Time per document | 110 s | 54 s | **40 s** |

**v3 is a measured model choice.** Per-stage cost tracking showed the coding agent was 56% of the cost. We tested cheaper models stage by stage on the same cases: Haiku 5.5 for triage and for the coding agent, and Sonnet 5.5 instead of Opus 5.5 for the verifier, kept 100% quality. Haiku 5.5 for extraction did not: it reported "no changes" for a real age-limit change, so extraction stays on Sonnet 5.5. The experiment also exposed a bug (a cut-off structured answer crashed instead of recovering), now fixed and unit tested. All runs: `evals/results/extra/v3a.json`, `v3b.json`, `v3c.json`.

Further runs (in `evals/results/extra/`):

- **A whole scheme from its founding order.** From an empty rulebook and only the real 28 June 2024 GR, Niyam recognised a new scheme, extracted 19 rules, wrote the rulebook and 34 tests, and passed **25 of 25** of our hand-written baseline test citizens, which it never saw ($0.81, 201 s, checkpoint `01M4JFNT0M069MG48K0FT9V50P`).
- **Consistency.** 9 more v2 runs on the three relevant cases: 100% on every metric, $0.61 per relevant order.
- **Recovery under injected failures.** A broken model output and an unusable text layer injected on purpose: both recovered, 100% outcomes.
- **A second real scheme.** On an operator's request (`--onboard`), Niyam encoded Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Anudan Yojana from the real 56-page 2019 consolidated GR ([PR #3](https://github.com/usv240/niyam-rulebook/pull/3), 49 tests, $1.54). Then the real 6 July 2023 order raising assistance to Rs 1,500 was judged **safe to merge alone** (only amounts rise, 16 of 16 checks agree, confidence 0.98, $0.20, dry run). Run live, the same order raised a question about widows with three or more children and went to a human ([PR #4](https://github.com/usv240/niyam-rulebook/pull/4)): 2 of 3 runs would have acted alone. Reviewing PR #3 caught a real mistake: a new `disabled` field defaulted to true, which would widen eligibility; fixed before merge. All four agent PRs are now reviewed: #2, #3 and #4 merged, #1 closed as superseded.
- **Acting alone.** A labelled synthetic order that only adds people: 2 of 2 runs decided to merge alone (dry run, never merged into the public rulebook). Every run on the real amendment, which removes some people, asked a human.

The improvement came from the neatlogs traces: in v1 the coordinator ruled three different ways on one test case and the job spent $3.05 before the budget stopped it. The root cause was that the benefit formula ("pay the difference") was missing from the context given to the verifier and coordinator. v2 adds it, plus a loop guard. # Night Shift

**The on-call engineer for your AI agents.** Built for neatHack 2026.

It stops the bleeding by itself, and only wakes you for decisions that can't be undone.

**Live:** https://web-emrq.vercel.app · sign in with GitHub · [SDK docs](https://web-emrq.vercel.app/docs) ·
[sandbox demo, no account needed](https://web-emrq.vercel.app/sandbox)

At 3 AM, a "harmless" change to a production AI agent starts failing. Maybe it pays refunds it
shouldn't, or reads docs from a folder that doesn't exist yet. Every request still returns HTTP 200.
Night Shift notices from the agent's neatlogs traces and the outcomes the agent reports. It then
investigates like a senior SRE: traces, deploy log, diff, and the **Entire checkpoint with the prompt
the coding agent was given**. It prices the damage with the **cfo.ai** unit economics, applies the
reversible fix your policy pre-approves, and proves the fix by having your agent replay the failed
runs. Then it pages you once: *handled, here's what it cost, and a permanent fix is waiting for your
approval in Slack.*

> Autonomous within a policy you set. A human approves anything irreversible (code-fix PRs, refunds,
> contacting customers, deleting data). Benchmark incidents are staged on purpose so they're
> reproducible; the Scout incidents ran live through the product.

## For judges: 60 seconds

| neatHack evidence | Where |
|---|---|
| **The agent completes a substantial task** | The whole incident lifecycle: detect → investigate → price → decide → contain → verify → report. Live on two agents: Harbor ([6/6 benchmark](evidence/benchmark/)) and Scout ([two live incidents](evidence/scout/)) |
| **Agent improved (before/after with numbers)** | [`evidence/before-after.md`](evidence/before-after.md): run 1 → run 3, from 4/6 to 6/6 handled correctly, after fixes based on what run 1 showed |
| **Recovers from failures** | Every incident is a failure it recovers from. If a fix fails verification, Night Shift undoes it ([`runner.py`](backend/nightshift/runner.py), test `test_failed_verification_undoes_action`). It survived neatlogs losing most of Scout's traces ([`evidence/scout/`](evidence/scout/README.md#what-we-learned-and-changed)) |
| **Used neatlogs** | Every agent run and every investigation is traced. Night Shift reads traces back over the neatlogs MCP during investigations, and creates a neatlogs detection after an attack. [`evidence/neatlogs.md`](evidence/neatlogs.md) |
| **Used Entire** | Every bad release was written by a separate Claude Code session with an Entire checkpoint. Night Shift resolves commit → checkpoint → prompt → the coding agent's own warning, plus entire-graph change lists. [`evidence/entire.md`](evidence/entire.md) |
| **Used cfo.ai** | [Business plan in cfo.ai](https://app.cfo.ai/s/CsWafbQfu2U1y94W) (pricing, costs, revenue, runway: break-even M08, runway > 24 months) and [customer unit economics in cfo.ai](https://app.cfo.ai/s/fHcCAy2lG_aXs3Qt), which Night Shift uses to price every incident. [`business/PLAN.md`](business/PLAN.md) |
| **Built in public** | #neatHack posts, drafted in [`posts/`](posts) |
| **Code written during the hackathon** | Commit history (first commit is the plan only), build log in [`hackathon.md`](hackathon.md) |

## The product

| | |
|---|---|
| **Connect an agent** | A 5-step wizard: name it → add the SDK → paste your neatlogs key (Night Shift finds your traces) → what a bad run costs → go live |
| **SDK** (`pip install nightshift-sdk`) | Zero dependencies and fails open. Your agent reads its release, model, step cap and kill switches from Night Shift. It reports deploys and graded outcomes, and runs verification replays. [`sdk/python/`](sdk/python) |
| **Agent page** | Live metrics, the control plane Night Shift steers, deploys (one-click redeploy), traces, a versioned policy editor, economics, credentials |
| **Incident inbox** | Timeline of the investigation, root cause → commit → Entire checkpoint → prompt, $ at risk, replay results, Approve and Undo, and the postmortem Night Shift writes |
| **Slack app** | One message per incident, updated as it works, with **Approve fix** and **Undo** buttons. Approving a code fix opens a revert PR on your repo with the postmortem and a regression eval |
| **Policy** | YAML per agent: confidence and money gates, which reversible actions it may take alone, and what always needs a human. The API rejects any "auto" action that isn't reversible |

## How it works

```
 your agent ──(neatlogs SDK traces)──► neatlogs ◄──(MCP read-back)───┐
     │  ▲                                                             │
     │  └── nightshift-sdk: release · model · flags · step cap        │
     └────► outcomes, deploys, replay results ──► NIGHT SHIFT ────────┘
                                                   1 WATCH       failures, tool errors, escalations, loops, cost
                                                   2 INVESTIGATE Claude Sonnet + tools: traces, deploy log, diff,
                                                                 Entire checkpoint → prompt, entire-graph
                                                   3 PRICE       $/min × minutes until a human answers (cfo.ai)
                                                   4 DECIDE      your policy: reversible? confident? worth waking you?
                                                   5 CONTAIN     roll back · fail over model · kill switch · cap steps
                                                   6 VERIFY      your agent replays the failed runs; live metrics; auto-undo
                                                   7 REPORT      Slack/ntfy/webhook · postmortem · regression eval · fix PR on approval
```

Spec: [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) · deploy: [`docs/DEPLOY.md`](docs/DEPLOY.md) ·
demo script: [`docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md`](docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md)

## Results

- **Harbor benchmark** ([`evidence/benchmark/run3-live`](evidence/benchmark/)): six staged incidents
  (unchecked refunds, tool schema drift, flaky-dependency loop, provider outage, prompt-injection
  wave, ticket flood). All six were handled correctly. Five were contained autonomously 13–21 s after
  detection and verified by replay; the low-impact one was deferred to the morning without paging
  anyone. Each investigation cost $0.05–0.15.
- **Scout, live through the product** ([`evidence/scout/`](evidence/scout/)): a bad release written by
  a Claude Code session. Detected about 1.5 min after deploy, rolled back automatically, verified by
  replays Scout ran itself (3/3), resolved in under 3 min. The postmortem quotes the coding agent's
  ignored warning, found through Entire.

## Run it locally

```bash
cp .env.example .env            # LITELLM_API_KEY, NEATLOGS_API_KEY
scripts/dev.sh                  # API on :8000 + web on :3000 (local dev mode, no sign-in)
scripts/dev.sh sim              # offline deterministic brain, no keys needed

cd backend && uv run pytest     # 26 tests
uv run python -m bench.benchmark --brain live           # incident benchmark (~$1.5 of gateway credit)
uv run --project backend python agents/scout/scout.py eval --release s3   # Scout's offline eval
```

Entire checkpoints are on GitHub as `_entire/*` branches (the build sandbox could only push
branches). `scripts/restore_entire_refs.sh` moves them to `refs/entire/*`.

## Repo map

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `backend/nightshift/` | Detector, investigator, provenance (git + Entire + entire-graph), impact, policy, actions, verifier, reporter, adapters, neatlogs sources |
| `backend/product/` | Workspaces, agents, encrypted secrets, Slack app, paging, GitHub fix PRs, repo clones |
| `backend/api/` | FastAPI: product API, SDK endpoints, Slack endpoints, sandbox, SSE |
| `sdk/python/` | `nightshift-sdk` |
| `backend/harbor/` | Harbor, the refunds support agent (releases r42–r46 written by coding-agent sessions) |
| `agents/scout/` | Scout, the docs assistant, connected only through the SDK and neatlogs |
| `web/` | Next.js: site, app, docs, sandbox |
| `business/` | Unit economics, business plan (mirrors cfo.ai), Ari prompts |
| `deploy/` | GCP VM (Caddy HTTPS), Vercel env, Slack manifest |
| `evidence/` | Benchmark runs, before/after, Scout incidents, neatlogs and Entire evidence |

## Honest limitations

- Harbor's customers are simulated from a scenario bank, and its tools act on a sandbox ledger. Scout
  answers questions from a fixed bank about a fictional product.
- Harbor's provider outage is injected in our gateway client, and the prompt-injection traffic is generated.
- The `sim` brain exists for offline demos and tests and is never used for evidence.
- Permanent fixes are proposed as PRs, never merged by Night Shift: shipping code is a human decision by design.
- Night Shift currently ships a Python SDK only; other agents can call the HTTP API.claude/settings.json

## Project
**Night Shift** — the on-call engineer for AI agents. It detects incidents in a production LLM agent,
traces them to the change and the coding-agent prompt that caused them, prices the damage, takes
reversible containment actions from a pre-approved policy, verifies the fix by replaying failed
conversations, and pages a human only for irreversible decisions.

# Storybound **A story agent that keeps its promises, and can prove it.** A child's drawing and a lesson go in. The agent writes an **oath** (a list of promises), checks every page against it **before the child sees it**, rewrites any page that breaks a promise, and ships a **receipt** for the grown-ups. Then: pictures and narration, a **quiz** whose every question is verified against the story, a picture-order game, a read-along **video** made from the finished story, and grown-up-written promises. Built for neatHack (10 to 12 Oct 2026) with neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai. > Why it is not just a chat model with a good prompt: in our 84-run experiment the same writer shipped at least one broken promise in **27 of 28 stories** when ungated and in **27 of 28** when it reviewed its own story, and in **0 of 28** when an independent gate checked every page ([report](evidence/reports/20261010-1505-IST-sweep-2-p2.md)). Most broken promises were quality failures (answer position, lesson missing, reading level), not safety failures. ## Does it fit the problem statement? *"Build an AI agent, or a team of agents, that completes a substantial task from start to finish. Give it a goal, tools and an environment; let each result guide its next action."* **Yes**, in four lines (full case with evidence and limits: [docs/QUALIFICATION.md](docs/QUALIFICATION.md)): - **Goal, tools, environment:** a drawing and a lesson become an oath (a checkable list of promises); tools are vision, a writer, an independent judge from another model family, pictures, voice, deterministic checkers and a video renderer; the environment is a LangGraph run with state, quotas, budgets and a child using a real web app. - **Each result guides the next action:** a failed check rewrites that page; a judge's quoted objection rolls the run back to that page; a quota error waits and retries, then degrades that page to text and says so; a quiz question that cannot be verified is dropped; a movie scene that fails its own checks is repaired. Gated, the same writer shipped a broken promise in **0 of 28** stories after fixing breaks on 19 first passes (1.82 repairs per story); ungated or self-reviewing, **27 of 28**. - **Substantial, start to finish:** drawing, safety screen, character, oath, eight verified pages, whole-story check, verified quiz, pictures, narration, receipt, then a read-along movie, with no human step in between. - **Said plainly:** it is a bounded agentic workflow (a fixed stage order with open-ended repair inside it, by design for children's content), not an open-ended tool-picking agent; the judge is not a human; samples are small. ## What it looks like The web app, desktop width. Screens marked *live* came from a real story run through the browser (`web/scripts/e2e-real.mjs`, real models); screens marked *demo mode* come from the free scripted mode (`?mock=1`), which shows the same screens without calling any model. The drawings are test fixtures or drawn by the test script, never a real child's. | | | | --- | --- | | ![Draw your hero](docs/img/01-draw.png)

**7. The receipt for grown-ups, promise by promise** (demo mode) | ![The read-along movie, title card](docs/img/08-movie-drawing.png)

# Spend Radar **An agent that tells a finance team where competitors out-invest them in people, and shows its work.** Every number in its report has a source, and before reporting, the agent tries to disprove its own findings. Built solo by team **qwep** (Akarsh Dhingra) during **neatHack**, 10–12 Oct 2026. Uses **neatlogs** (tracing), **Entire** (checkpoints + code graph) and **cfo.ai** (business plan). > The company in the demo, *Acme Observability Inc.*, is **fictional**. Its finance files are generated by `scripts/make_acme_data.py`. The competitors are real; their data comes live from Crustdata. Sample output: [`evidence/sample-report/report.md`](evidence/sample-report/report.md) (evidence run 1010-7bf26d). ## The problem Finance teams budget against their own ledger, not the market. They find out a competitor doubled its ML team, or that their own marketing team is out of line with peers, a quarter too late. The data exists (headcount by function, hiring, funding), but turning it into a budget comparison you can defend takes days of manual work. ## What the agent does, end to end **Input:** a folder of finance files (a budget spreadsheet, invoice PDFs, a spend policy, a salary table) and a list of competitors. **Output:** `runs//report.md`, which contains: - **per category** (engineering, ML/AI, sales, marketing): Acme's share of headcount vs the competitor median range, whether the policy is met, and the gap in people and dollars (an estimate) - **internal checks:** budget and invoice totals that don't add up, mis-categorised invoices, infra invoices over budget - an **Overturned claims** section, listing findings the agent disproved itself - a numbered **source for every number** (file + sheet/row/page, or Crustdata endpoint + field + fetch time) - the **recovery log** (what failed, the options, what the LLM chose, and what a fixed rule would have chosen) ## How it works ![Spend Radar loop](evidence/architecture.png) ```mermaid flowchart LR P[PLAN
LLM writes typed task list] --> C{coverage check} C --> A[ACT
one tool call] A --> O[OBSERVE
store value + source] O --> V{VERIFY
deterministic checks} V -- pass --> A V -- fail --> D[DECIDE:RECOVERY
LLM picks from fixed menu] D --> A A -- queue empty --> X[cross-document checks] X --> F[FINDINGS
maths in Python] F --> S[SELF-AUDIT
recompute · sources · contradictions
LLM verdict + 2nd-provider opinion] S --> R[REPORT
sourced, overturned claims listed] ``` **Who decides what.** - **The LLM decides:** the plan, which recovery action to take from a fixed menu (`reparse_alt`, `narrow_range`, `fetch_more_signal`, `substitute_competitor`, `mark_low_confidence`, `skip`), and the audit verdicts. - **Python decides:** how tasks run, **all arithmetic**, retry caps (3 per task), Crustdata credit caps (60 per run), and LLM quota. | Focus area | How it shows up | Trace | |---|---|---| | Planning | `plan` span: an LLM task list validated against a Pydantic schema; `verify:plan_coverage` adds anything the plan missed | `288f07d84bb84e15754a241eef40d779` | | Tool use | list_files, read_spreadsheet, read_pdf (text / LLM), crustdata_company, crustdata_jobs, classify_titles; each is a `TOOL` span | same | | State | `RunState` saved atomically after every step (`runs//state.json`) | — | | Context | every figure keeps its source; the report cites them | — | | Execution | one tool per task; tasks whose inputs aren't ready are deferred | — | | Recovery | `decide:recovery` spans record the options offered, the choice, the rule default, and the reason; fallback across models/providers; Crustdata backoff + stale-cache fallback; resume after a crash | `evidence/recovery/` | | Verification | totals within 1%, ≥ 2 independent signals, signal agreement, vendor-category consistency, no unsourced numbers | `verify:*` spans | | Iteration | case studies with before/after runs | `evidence/case-studies/` | **Confidence is computed, never typed in:** `confidence = checks × signals × freshness` (`spendradar/verify.py`). - `checks` = passed / total checks behind the finding. - `signals` = min(1, n_signals / 2) × agreement between signals. - `freshness` = 1 up to 90 days old, falling to 0.5 at 365 days. - An audit downgrade halves the score; an overturn sets it to 0. ## How we used the three tools ### neatlogs: tracing is the debugger - Every Gemini call is auto-traced (`instrumentations=["google_genai"]`). OpenRouter calls, tool calls, `verify:*`, `decide:recovery`, `fallback:`, `audit:` and `fault:injected:*` are custom spans. - Runs are tagged `sha:`, `run:`, `variant:

## Results so far

All numbers come from scorecards in [`evidence/evals/`](evidence/evals/).

| Run | Commit | Planted errors caught | Unsupported numbers | Peers kept | Crustdata credits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1010-b31657 (before fix) | 11a5108 | 5/5 | 0 | 2/5 | 26.6 |
| 1010-7bf26d (after fix, evidence) | 22f00b0 | 5/5 | 0 | 5/5 | 5.4 |
| 5 evidence runs on gpt-5-nano, 0 fallback hops | bb61e37 | 5/5 in all 5 | 0 | 5/5 | 0 (cached) |
| fixture run (Sentry marketing ×5 planted) | bb61e37 | 6/6 | 0 | 5/5 | 0 (cached) |

**Held-out companies** ([case study 04](evidence/case-studies/04-held-out-companies.md)): six more fictional companies in five other industries, built after the agent and never used to tune it. The latest finished run of all seven companies catches every planted error with 0 false alarms (`summary` in [`evidence/frontend_data.json`](evidence/frontend_data.json); per-run values in [`evidence/evals/README.md`](evidence/evals/README.md)). Fault-injected runs (Crustdata 429 + LLM 429) on Acme, Ledgerly and Bastion still caught every planted error.

Case studies (each n = 1 per side unless stated, with caveats):
- [01: reasoning calls took ~2 minutes each](evidence/case-studies/01-unbounded-llm-latency.md). Mean reasoning-call latency went from 120.9 s to 6.5 s after adding a per-call timeout with fallback.
- [02: one weak category threw away 3 of 5 peers](evidence/case-studies/02-competitor-substitution.md). Substitutions went from 3 to 0, and credits from 26.6 to 5.4.
- [04: held-out companies](evidence/case-studies/04-held-out-companies.md). Exposed a missing duplicate-invoice check, a missed one-off mis-categorised invoice, Windows path bugs and an audit that ignored its own line-item check. Acme's mis-categorised invoice after that last fix: caught in 3 of 3 runs (before: 1 of 2).
- [03: bugs that only showed on fallback models](evidence/case-studies/03-fallback-model-quality.md). Runs that crashed went from 1/3 to 0/3, and the mis-categorised invoice from caught 0/3 to 3/3 on the main model.

Paid-equivalent cost per run (n = 5, gpt-5-nano): **$0.0285 LLM** (range $0.0270–$0.0296) **+ 20.8 Crustdata credits** with no cache.

## See the evidence

[`site/`](site/) is a static site built from every scored run (`site/data.js`, regenerated by `python -m spendradar export`). Open `site/index.html` in a browser; no server needed. It shows the generalisation matrix across 7 companies, findings the self-audit overturned, a step-by-step replay of each run, every recovery decision, before/after pairs from the case studies, the cfo.ai numbers and all neatlogs trace IDs. Design system: Audit Console; the Motion switch in the top bar turns the animations off.

## Run it yourself

```bash
uv sync                                  # Python 3.12
cp .env.example .env                     # NEATLOGS_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, CRUSTDATA_API_KEY
uv run python scripts/make_acme_data.py  # regenerate the fictional data (already committed)
uv run python -m spendradar run data/acme             # full run → runs/<id>/report.md
uv run python -m spendradar run data/acme --evidence  # LLM cache off, tagged as evidence
uv run python -m spendradar run data/acme --inject crustdata:429 --inject llm:429
uv run python -m spendradar run data/acme --crash-after-step 15 && uv run python -m spendradar resume <id>
uv run python -m spendradar eval --n 3 --evidence     # scorecard → evidence/evals/ + a spendradar_eval trace in neatlogs (-

# VendorLens — AI vendor due-diligence agent Built for **neatHack 2026** (team `solohackaton`, solo). Give it a company domain; an AI agent plans an OSINT investigation, executes tools step by step, recovers from failures, verifies claims, and writes a **cited risk brief** (score + evidence + sources). ## Architecture ``` +-------------------+ | planner (LLM) | JSON plan: 4-8 tool steps, +--------+----------+ cheapest high-signal first | +--------v----------+ | executor + state | persistent state dict across steps +--------+----------+ per-step retry w/ backoff | +--------------+--------------+ | | | +--------v-----+ +------v------+ +-----v------+ | tools | | observer | | risk | | crustdata | | (LLM) | | scoring | | dns / whois | | replans on | | weighted | | tls / home | | surprises | | signals | | web search | +-------------+ +-----+------+ +--------------+ | +-------v-------+ | cited brief | | brief.md | +---------------+ Every step -> neatlogs spans (LLM auto-traced) + trace.jsonl evidence Every commit -> Entire checkpoint (session context behind the change) Business plan -> cfo.ai (pricing, costs, revenue, runway) Browser verdict -> jev-web typed-decision model, 100% on-device ``` ## Quickstart ```bash pip install -r requirements.txt cp .env.example .env # fill in keys (or run --demo with none) # Full agent run, canned data, no keys needed: python -m vendorlens acme-cloud-services.example --demo # Live run (needs LITELLM_* in .env): python -m vendorlens example-vendor.com # Artifacts land in runs/// : brief.md, state.json, trace.jsonl ``` ## The three mandatory tools (and their roles) 1. **neatlogs** — `vendorlens/tracing.py` follows the official setup guide: `neatlogs.init(api_key=...)` once, `neatlogs.wrap(OpenAI())` so every planner/observer model call is traced (model, messages, latency, tokens). Tool executions are logged as structured events to `trace.jsonl` (evidence). Signup is manual: app.neatlogs.com -> Settings -> API keys -> **Project** API key (top one, NOT the `nlw_` key) -> `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`. 2. **Entire** — `entire/setup.sh` + `entire/ENTIRE.md`. Run setup, sign in with GitHub in the browser, import `warsang/vendorlens`, then commit: each commit links to the agent session behind it (`entire checkpoint list`, `entire checkpoint explain HEAD`). Include the checkpoint link + ID in the submission. 3. **cfo.ai** — `docs/business-plan-inputs.md` has the full inputs (pricing tiers, unit economics, revenue scenarios, runway). Sign up at https://cfo.ai/neathacks (**a card is required; cancel immediately in Settings -> Billing**), paste the inputs, include the resulting plan. ## Demo page (jev-web verdict layer) `demo/` is a static page: paste vendor homepage text, hit **Assess**, and a Bekko 17m typed-decision model scores scam risk **in the browser** — zero network requests after weights load, no text leaves the device. ```bash cd demo && npm install /home/hatch/workspace/jev-web/jev-web-0.7.2.tgz npx serve . # open the page it prints ``` ## Evidence checklist (mapped to judging criteria) | Criterion (weight) | Evidence | |---|---| | The agent 30% | `brief.md` + `state.json` from a live run; failure->retry->recovery visible in `trace.jsonl` | | Use of neatlogs/Entire/cfo.ai 25% | neatlogs trace links (before/after runs); Entire checkpoint link + ID; cfo.ai business plan | | Demo video 20% | `docs/demo-script.md` — 2:45 outline explicitly covering all three tools | | Building in public 15% | `docs/build-in-public.md` — drafted #neatHack posts (DRAFTS, need approval) | | Usefulness/originality 10% | cited risk briefs + on-device private scoring | ## Repo & submission - Public repo: `warsang/vendorlens` (commits must fall within Oct 10–12). - Submission: quote post of the official neatlogs X post with team, name, project, repo and demo link, in the Oct 12 7:00–11:55 PM IST window. ## Notes on live tools - `dns_lookup` (UDP/53), `whois_lookup` (TCP/43) and `tls_inspect` (direct TCP/443) need unrestricted internet. They fail gracefully (recorded as failed steps; the agent continues) in restricted sandboxes. - `fetch_homepage` and `web_search_reports` use httpx and honor proxy env vars. If you hit `Invalid port: ':1]'`, your `no_proxy` contains `[::1]` which httpx misparses — override with: `export no_proxy='localhost,127.0.0.1,::1,198.19.0.1,198.19.0.2'`. - `--demo` mode runs the whole loop with canned data and no keys. ## Next steps (pick up here) **1. Signups — all on you (nothing here needs them to build, everything needs them to run live):** - **neatlogs**: sign up at app.neatlogs.com, create a project, put the Project API key (the top key, not `nlw_`) in `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`. Traces must exist for the submission. - **Entire**: run `entire/setup.sh`, sign in with GitHub in the browser, import `warsang/vendorlens`, commit, and capture your first checkpoint — you need the checkpoint **link + ID** for the submission. - **cfo.ai**: sign up at cfo.ai/neathacks — a card is required, **cancel immediately** in Settings → Billing (their own instructions; you won't be billed). Then paste `docs/business-plan-inputs.md` into cfo.ai and export the resulting business plan. - **LiteLLM shared key**: grab it from the check-in email or the Discord → `LITELLM_API_BASE`, `LITELLM_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MODEL` in `.env`. $20 budget for the team, keep prompts tight. - **Crustdata**: app.crustdata.com, promo code `NEATLOGS-OCT2026`, **email signup (not "Continue with Google")** so the code applies → `CRUSTDATA_API_KEY`. 5,000 credits. **2. Run it:** `./setup.sh` first (interactive, writes a gitignored `.env` — keys never touch the repo). Then `python -m vendorlens ` for a live investigation, `python -m vendorlens --no-llm` for live tools with a deterministic plan and no LLM key, or `python -m vendorlens acme.example --demo` for the canned no-keys run. No LLM.env.example .gitignore README.md demo/README.md demo/index.html demo/package-lock.json demo/package.json demo/vendor/jev-web-0.7.2.tgz docs/AGENT_ONBOARDING.md docs/build-in-public.md docs/business-plan-inputs.md docs/business-plan.pdf docs/demo-script.md entire/ENTIRE.md entire/setup.sh requirements.txt setup.sh vendorlens/__init__.py vendorlens/__main__.py vendorlens/agent.py vendorlens/brief.py vendorlens/llm.py vendorlens/risk.py vendorlens/tools/__init__.py vendorlens/tools/crustdata.py vendorlens/tools/dns_tool.py vendorlens/tools/homepage.py vendorlens/tools/tls_tool.py vendorlens/tools/websearch.py vendorlens/tools/whois_tool.py vendorlens/tracing.py # ReleaseCrew Give it a GitHub repo and a release tag. A small crew of agents ships the launch story: a **verified** changelog, an X thread, and a short trailer. Invented features get rejected. Failed runs resume. Built during **neatHack Oct 10–12**. ```bash npx tsx src/cli.ts --repo honojs/hono --tag v4.13.12 --from v4.13.11 --out examples/hono-v4.13.12 ``` Example kit: [`examples/hono-v4.13.12`](./examples/hono-v4.13.12) (Hono `v4.13.11...v4.13.12`), written by `claude-haiku` through the neatHack LiteLLM proxy and traced in neatlogs. | Hono run (real LLM, exported to neatlogs) | Before (`--demo-failures`) | After (clean) | | --- | --- | --- | | Spans | 23 | 17 | | Retries / errors | 3 / 1 | 0 / 0 | | Writer attempts | 2 (verifier caught an invented feature) | 1 | | Tokens (real usage) | 7,989 | 4,430 (−45%) | | Wall time | 20.8s | 17.6s | Details and trace links: [`evidence/neatlogs/comparison.md`](./evidence/neatlogs/comparison.md). ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD CLI["CLI: repo + tag"] --> Coord["Coordinator
durable .releasecrew state"] Coord --> Planner["Planner"] Coord --> Research["Researcher"] Research --> GH["GitHub API
commits · PRs · compare"] Coord --> Writer["Writer"] Writer --> Verifier["Verifier / guardrail"] Verifier -->|unsupported claim| Writer Verifier -->|pass| Media["Media"] Media --> FFMPEG["ffmpeg trailer"] Coord --> Kit["Release kit
notes.md · thread.txt · trailer.mp4 · evidence.json"] Coord --> Neat["neatlogs spans
+ local JSONL traces"] Writer --> AISDK["AI SDK or heuristic fallback"] Dev["This repo, while building"] --> Entire["Entire checkpoints
+ entire-graph"] Inputs["docs/business-plan-inputs.md"] --> CFO["cfo.ai business plan"] ``` | Agent | Job | | --- | --- | | Coordinator | Runs the crew, writes state after every step, resumes `--resume ` | | Planner | Breaks “ship this tag” into research → write → verify → media → assemble | | Researcher | Reads releases, compare, commits, merged PRs | | Writer | Drafts `notes.md` and `thread.txt` from the change list only | | Verifier | Grounds every bullet in SHAs, PR numbers, files, or official notes | | Media | Storyboard + PPM slides + ffmpeg. Falls back if the first encoder dies | Deliberate recoveries, all visible in traces: 1. **Rate limit** — first GitHub call can throw a demo 429; `withRetry` backs off. 2. **Bad model output** — first writer pass can inject a hallucinated feature; the verifier rejects it; the writer retries with feedback. 3. **Render failure** — first ffmpeg attempt can use a fake encoder; the next attempt uses libx264 / a simpler encode. ## How to run Needs Node 20+ and `ffmpeg` on `PATH`. ```bash cp .env.example .env # add keys if you have them npm install npx tsx src/cli.ts --repo owner/name --tag vX.Y.Z --from vX.Y.Z-1 --out ./output ``` Useful flags: | Flag | What it does | | --- | --- | | `--demo-failures` | Force the three recoveries above | | `--compare-baseline` | Run a sloppy pass, then a clean pass, write `evidence/neatlogs/{before,after}.json` | | `--resume ` | Continue `.releasecrew/runs/` after a crash | | `--run-id ` | Stable id for traces and state | ```bash npm test npm run typecheck npx neatlogs doctor --local --json ``` ### Keys None of these block a local kit. The researcher talks to the public GitHub API. The writer has a GitHub-grounded heuristic fallback. | Key | Role | | --- | --- | | `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` | Export spans to the neatlogs dashboard. Without it: local JSONL only | | `LITELLM_API_KEY` + `LITELLM_BASE_URL` (neatHack: `https://litellm.vision.aivar.app/v1`, default model `claude-haiku`) / `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY` / Bedrock | LLM planner + writer via the AI SDK (`wrapAISDK`) | | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | Higher GitHub rate limit | | cfo.ai | Owner signup (card, then cancel). Not an env var | See [`.env.example`](./.env.example) and [`docs/neatlogs.md`](./docs/neatlogs.md). ## Partner roles (required) ### neatlogs — observe and improve the crew `src/telemetry/neatlogs.ts` calls `init()`, `span()`, `trace()`, `log()`, `flush()`, `shutdown()`. Agent steps, GitHub/ffmpeg tools, verifier guardrails, LLM calls, and retries each get a span. `neatlogs/ai` wraps the AI SDK when a model key exists. Without `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`, the same tree is written to `.releasecrew/runs//trace.jsonl` and copied under `evidence/neatlogs/` so judges can still compare numbers. ### Entire — repository context while building Entire is the **dev-workflow** partner, not a runtime dependency of a release kit. - `entire enable --agent cursor` + git-refs checkpoints - `entire plugin install graph` + `entire graph init-agents` - Search / impact / snapshot committed under [`evidence/entire/`](./evidence/entire) I used `entire graph search` to find the durable store and `entire graph impact --symbol verifyDraft` before changing the guardrail. ### cfo.ai — plan the business Not in the agent loop. [`docs/business-plan-inputs.md`](./docs/business-plan-inputs.md) is paste-ready (pricing, COGS, revenue, runway, scenarios). [`docs/business-plan.md`](./docs/business-plan.md) summarizes the plan (Indie $29 / Team $149 / Launch $499, $2.7k → $36.9k MRR over 18 months, 92–93% gross margin, cash never negative and ending at ~$178k, LTV:CAC ~9–10x).
